question: Quebec General Election Winner
resolution_criteria:
Parliamentary elections to elect all 127 seats of the National Assembly of Quebec are scheduled to take place in Quebec on October 5, 2026.

This market will resolve to the political party that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Quebec as a result of this election.

If voting in the 2026 Quebec general election does not occur by January 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie for the most seats won between this party and any other, this market will resolve in favor of the party that won the most valid votes in the respective election. If this also results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose listed abbreviation comes first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Élections Québec (https://www.electionsquebec.qc.ca).

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
As of September 18, 2026, the Parti Québécois (PQ) led every poll in the campaign but one, and the prediction markets I found priced it as the clear favourite. Nothing I found settles the question as of September 19. I left out everything published after that date, including search results that described the outcome.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria name Élections Québec (electionsquebec.qc.ca) as the fallback if credible reporting is ambiguous. I did not fetch it, because anything it shows now would postdate the September 19 cutoff. As of September 19 there were no results yet; voting day was October 5, 2026.
- 2026-08-27: The Lieutenant Governor dissolved the legislature and issued the election writs on Premier Christine Fréchette's advice, with voting set for 2026-10-05. 127 seats; 64 are needed for a majority. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Quebec_general_election)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settled the question by September 19. Voting had not happened yet, and the PQ led most polls by about 4 to 9 points.
- Party leaders: Christine Fréchette (CAQ, since 2026-04-12), Charles Milliard (Liberals, PLQ, since 2026-02-13), Paul St-Pierre Plamondon (PQ), Ruba Ghazal (Québec solidaire, QS), Éric Duhaime (Conservatives, PCQ). [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Quebec_general_election)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
Polls are listed by date as given on Wikipedia, in this order: CAQ / PLQ / PQ / QS / PCQ. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Quebec_general_election)
- 2026-09-17: Pallas: 22/22/28/11/16. Segma: 22/19/29/12/18.
- 2026-09-16: Third debate, hosted by Noovo.
- 2026-09-15: Second debate, hosted by TVA.
- 2026-09-14: Nanos: 21/24/28/9/16.
- 2026-09-13: Five polls:
  - Léger: 21/23/29/10/17.
  - Research Co.: 23/22/28/10/16.
  - Synopsis: 24/22/28/11/14.
  - Mainstreet: 28/22/24/8/17. This is the only poll with the CAQ ahead.
  - Pallas (09-12): 23/23/27/11/16.
- 2026-09-09: First debate, hosted by Radio-Canada. St-Pierre Plamondon pledged a sovereignty referendum even without a PQ majority.
- 2026-09-06: Léger: 23/22/29/10/15. Pallas (09-05): 24/20/29/11/15.
- Late August: Léger (08-30): 24/22/29/10/15. Pallas (08-29): 24/22/29/9/16. Synopsis (08-26): 27/20/28/10/14. Léger (08-24): 23/23/30/7/16.
- Early August: Léger (08-09): 20/24/30/11/13. Pallas (08-02): 19/27/31/9/14.
- Trend: the PQ held steady at about 27 to 31%. The CAQ recovered from about 20% under Fréchette, then dipped in mid-September. The PLQ hovered around 22%, and the PCQ rose to about 16 to 18%.
- 2026-04-13: Coverage said Fréchette faced a tight deadline to revive the CAQ. At one point Qc125 projected the CAQ at zero seats. [National Newswatch](https://nationalnewswatch.com/2026/04/13/with-elections-near-quebec-premier-designate-under-tight-deadline-to-revive-caq)
- 2025-12-03: A Léger poll had the PQ at 39%, leading in every region. [Qc125](https://www.qc125.ca/p/le-plq-seffondre-le-pq-bondit)

## 4. Base rates
- Recent winners: PQ (2012, a narrow minority), PLQ (2014), CAQ (2018 and 2022). The CAQ held a large majority after 2022.
- In 2012 the PQ's lead in polls shrank to a narrow plurality. Leads of 4 to 6 points in multi-party races have sometimes narrowed in the final weeks, as in 2012 and 2018.
- The PQ's francophone vote is efficient: its support is concentrated where seats are won. That favours it winning the most seats even on about 28 to 29% of the vote.
- I did not compute a formal historical rate for "the poll leader three weeks out wins the most seats".

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-08: A Qc125 update was reported to give PQ 54 seats, PLQ 31 and CAQ 24. It put the chance of a PQ majority at about 17% and of a PQ plurality at about 70%. I saw these figures only in a search summary and could not verify the original article. [Qc125](https://www.qc125.ca/p/mise-a-jour-qc125-ya-pas-de-point)
- 2026-08-28: 338Canada projected PQ 48 seats (range 29-69), PLQ 31, CAQ 28, PCQ 11 and QS 9. It put the PQ's chance of a plurality at 68%. [338Canada](https://mail.338canada.com/quebec)
- Prediction markets: [Prediction Hunt](https://prediction.com/news/caq-win-probability-falls-12-points-as-bettors-sep-13-2026), [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/quebec-general-election-winner)
  - 2026-07-31: PQ at 55% on Kalshi and 61% on Polymarket.
  - 2026-08-21: PQ at about 72% (platform not named).
  - 2026-08-28: PLQ at 6% (platform not named).
  - 2026-09-13: CAQ at 22% on Polymarket and 24% on Kalshi.
  - 2026-09-15: CAQ at about 14% (platform not named).
  - An aggregator snapshot dated around 08-12 had the PQ at 76% on Polymarket.
- I found no price for "Party A" and no Manifold market.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-23: Fourth and final debate, on Radio-Canada. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Quebec_general_election)
- Late September to early October: more polls from Léger, Pallas, Segma, Mainstreet and others, plus updated Qc125 and 338Canada projections.
- The referendum pledge is a possible risk for the PQ. The rise of the PCQ and the CAQ's possible collapse could reshape vote splits seat by seat.
- 2026-10-05: Election day. Results are expected that night.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- The PQ led every poll except one in late August through mid-September: Léger 29 (Sept 13), Pallas 28 (Sept 17), Segma 29 (Sept 17), Nanos 28 (Sept 14).
- Mainstreet (Sept 13) is the outlier, with the CAQ ahead 28 to 24.
- 338Canada (Aug 28) gave the PQ a 68% chance of a plurality, and Qc125 (about Sept 8) gave about 70% plurality plus 17% majority, roughly 87% for most seats.
- Prediction markets: the CAQ fell from about 22-24% (Sept 13) to about 14% (Sept 15), which implies the PQ around 70%.

(e) **Upset scenario:** The PQ's referendum pledge, which applies even without a majority, triggers late federalist consolidation. Soft PQ and CAQ voters break toward the CAQ under Fréchette or toward the Liberals. The PQ falls to about 25% and the CAQ wins a plurality on efficient suburban and regional seats. Alternatively, the Liberals plus a vote split could push the PLQ to the most seats. The PCQ surging in the Quebec City region would mostly scramble the seat counts rather than win outright.

**Reasoning:** I anchored on the markets and models (PQ about 68-75%). I trimmed that slightly for Quebec's history of late shifts and for the Mainstreet outlier. The CAQ, as the governing party, is the main alternative, with the PLQ just behind it.
